title: Subjects
Subjects
Observability
text:
@opentelemetry/api is a peer dependency. Applications register their own tracer and meter providers; without a provider, the instrumentation is a no-op.
Subject operations emit xstate.nats.subscribe, xstate.nats.message, xstate.nats.publish, and xstate.nats.request spans. NATS reconnect events emit xstate.nats.reconnect; KV watches emit xstate.nats.kv.watch and xstate.nats.kv.entry. Publish/request operations inject trace context into NATS headers; received messages extract it so traces can cross application boundaries.

title: Observability
text:
Lifecycle diagnostics
config: {
  opts: { servers: ['wss://your-nats.example'] },
  maxRetries: 3,
  diagnostics: { lifecycle: true },
}
When enabled, root transitions emit sanitized xstate.nats.lifecycle spans and console breadcrumbs with state, event type, server URLs, retry count, auth type, and manager readiness. Raw protocol debugging is separate from lifecycle diagnostics.

title: Observability
text:
Credential instrumentation
Credential load/refresh spans are xstate.nats.credentials.load and .refresh. Metrics are:







Metric
Kind




xstate.nats.credentials.operations
Counter by operation/outcome


xstate.nats.credentials.operation.duration
Duration histogram in milliseconds


xstate.nats.credentials.state.transitions
Counter by state



Set credentials.diagnostics: true for sanitized credential state/operation breadcrumbs. Credential contents and provider error messages are excluded from credential instrumentation. The browser demo’s State panel likewise summarizes state and counters without dumping auth configuration.

title: XState actors for NATS
text:
@jr200-labs/xstate-nats coordinates a NATS WebSocket connection, subject subscriptions, request/reply, key-value operations, and short-lived credentials using XState v5.
pnpm add @jr200-labs/xstate-nats xstate @opentelemetry/api
Start with the browser demo: configure a connection, subscribe, publish a message, and watch the active state. Its default sandbox needs no broker. Live mode connects directly from your browser to your own NATS WebSocket endpoint.

NATS still requires a server for real messaging. The hosted documentation and demo UI are static files; GitHub Pages does not host a broker. The sandbox adapter belongs only to the demo and is not shipped as part of the library.

title: Live demo
text: No NATS server runs in this browser. The default sandbox simulates messaging inside this tab. Real mode connects to a separate server that you provide. Open full screen.

title: Live demo
text:
Try recovery

Configure and connect. In Publish / subscribe, subscribe to a subject. For KV, select Real NATS, create a bucket in KV / watch, and subscribe to a key.
Open Recovery, choose subject or KV, and select Disconnect & reconnect. The client connection closes; active handles disappear, while the target configurations are retained. The library rebuilds them on the next connection.
Select Send verification value. The demo generates a unique value and only reports verified delivery when that value arrives through the restored subscription. Replayed historical KV entries cannot satisfy this check.
Back in the subscription controls, unsubscribe and watch the target and active maps clear. Subscribe again to see the child machine sync a new handle. Unsubscribe all clears that manager’s targets.

This walkthrough deliberately reconnects the client; it does not stop a broker or emulate a network outage. To explore a real outage, stop/restart your own disposable development broker while viewing the inspector. NATS applies maxReconnectAttempts; a final close enters the root’s closed state, from which Connect establishes a fresh connection and restores targets. Core subject messages missed while disconnected are not replayed.

title: Live demo
text:
Run the live recovery test
With a disposable local broker running with the repository’s nats-server.conf:
DEMO_NATS_WS=ws://127.0.0.1:42222 pnpm demo:test
This creates an isolated test bucket, verifies new KV delivery after reconnect, unsubscribes/resubscribes, and removes its bucket afterward. The documentation CI runs this against an ephemeral broker. Without the environment variable, the live test is skipped and browser sandbox tests still run.
See getting started to start a local WebSocket broker.

Getting started
text:
Run a local NATS broker
Install nats-server, then use the repository’s development configuration:
nats-server -c nats-server.conf
This enables JetStream and an unencrypted development WebSocket listener on port 42222. Preview the demo locally and select Real NATS · your server with ws://localhost:42222. The config has verbose development logging; use your own TLS, origin policy, and authentication for a deployed broker. See NATS WebSocket configuration.

title: Getting started
text:
Close and recover
actor.send({ type: 'DISCONNECT' })
// Wait for closed, then reconnect with the current configuration:
actor.send({ type: 'CONNECT' })
DISCONNECT drains and closes the connection. RESET is available in configured, closed, and error; it clears the root configuration. Send DISCONNECT and wait for closed before resetting an active session. Calling actor.stop() alone is not a replacement for disconnecting the broker connection.

title: Getting started
text:
Build the documentation
Use Node.js 22.12+ and the pnpm version in package.json. Install Quarto.
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm demo:dev              # browser demo at http://localhost:3001
quarto preview docs        # complete documentation site
quarto render docs         # static output in docs/_site
Quarto’s pre-render hook installs locked dependencies and builds the demo. Its relative asset paths work both locally and under the GitHub Pages project path. The Documentation workflow renders a preview on pull requests and publishes through the shared Quarto workflow after changes reach master.

title: Key-value
text: KV operations need a connected NATS server with JetStream enabled. They are available in the demo’s Real NATS · your server mode. The browser sandbox does not emulate JetStream.

title: Key-value
Key-value
Reference
text:
State
Meaning




not_configured
Waiting for CONFIGURE


configured
Configuration accepted; CONNECT starts a connection


connecting
Connection actor is running


initialise_managers
Waiting for subject and KV readiness


connected
Messaging events are forwarded to child managers


closing
Draining/closing and detaching managers


closed
Connection ended; current config can reconnect


error
Connection/close failed; inspect context.error



Use snapshot.matches(...) to check state. CONFIGURE during an active connection closes it and reconnects with the new configuration; during an in-flight connect it restarts that connect. CONNECT during closing queues a reconnect. A final NATS_CONNECTION.CLOSE clears the connection and manager readiness and enters closed.
NATS’s own reconnect settings live in config.opts. The root’s maxRetries field does not implement an automatic XState retry loop; failed connection attempts enter error and increment the retry count. Send CONNECT to retry from that state.

Event families







Family
Events




Connection
CONFIGURE, CONNECT, DISCONNECT, RESET, CREDENTIALS.RELOAD


Subjects
SUBJECT.SUBSCRIBE, SUBJECT.UNSUBSCRIBE, SUBJECT.UNSUBSCRIBE_ALL, SUBJECT.PUBLISH, SUBJECT.REQUEST

KV.BUCKET_CREATE, KV.BUCKET_DELETE, KV.BUCKET_LIST

KV.PUT, KV.GET, KV.DELETE, KV.SUBSCRIBE, KV.UNSUBSCRIBE, KV.UNSUBSCRIBE_ALL


Traffic
METRICS.RESET_UPLOAD, METRICS.RESET_DOWNLOAD, METRICS.RESET_ALL



Traffic reset events optionally select a metric source. Subject and KV child snapshots expose trafficMetrics; counters measure application payload bytes rather than total protocol wire traffic.

title: Reference
text:
Public exports
The package exports natsMachine, subjectManagerLogic, kvManagerLogic, credentialMachine, getCredentials, KvSubscriptionKey, parseNatsResult, credential and event/context types, and traffic metric helpers. See src/index.ts for the complete typed export surface.

title: Reference
text:
Error behavior
Connection failures are root errors. Subject request/publish failures use their result callbacks. KV operation failures use onResult; Subscription and watch setup/removal failures enter subject_error or kv_error. Inspect that child’s context.error (an aggregate with per-target causes). Successful handles remain active, failed removals retain their handles, and desired subscriptions remain available for retry. After fixing the underlying problem, disconnect and reconnect to restore subscriptions. Direct child users can send SUBJECT.CONNECT or KV.CONNECT to retry with their connection. A root connected state does not mean every operation succeeded.
The demo handles expected errors in its feedback area and Output panel. Its diagram intentionally shows the main lifecycle paths rather than every wildcard, reconfigure, and internal status transition.
